brief: Minimalistic variations of the user-selected Foldscape style, in the same warm palette, with fewer broad planes and PFP previews.

prompts.name: Essential
prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / minimal geometric artwork variation.
Input image: the supplied Foldscape artwork is the edit target and the approved visual direction.
Create a MUCH MORE MINIMAL variation of this exact Foldscape family, preserving its angular folded-plane character, asymmetric motion and warm vermilion/orange/oxblood color relationship.
Reduce the original many small facets to only a few large purposeful planes. No tiny facets, incidental slivers, hairline wedges, complicated folds or decorative outlines. Every edge and join should feel intentional. Broad clean negative space. Crisp flat vector-like artwork, no material texture, no gradients, no shading, no cast shadows or 3D rendering. Imply depth only through solid colors on front and return faces.
Use only three solid inks: vermilion #FF3300, orange #FF6600, deep oxblood #330000, plus the white background. The dark return faces should support the structure without becoming the dominant mass.
One centered standalone artwork on a pure-white square canvas. The entire shape should fit comfortably in the central 70–76% circular safe area, with even optical margins. No visible circle, text, labels, border, mockup, watermark, logo wordmark or presentation board.
Keep the art abstract: avoid an obvious letter, arrow, paper airplane, bird, mountain, gem, lightning bolt or stock crypto logo. Preserve the approved Foldscape's feeling of planes turning around an offset joint.
Variation A — ESSENTIAL: Keep the original upright, gently zigzagging gesture but reduce it to THREE broad folded panels, at most SIX visible colored faces total. A tall upper vermilion plane tips toward one orange middle plane; a shorter broad lower plane returns in the opposite direction. Use narrow oxblood return faces and two generous clear white seams. Remove all small fan blades from the original. The silhouette should feel like a calm distilled version of the supplied artwork, balanced and sculptural, with a small offset at the waist and a clear base. Minimal, precise and elegant.

Preserve one clearly readable diagonal white cleft through the center, not multiple intersecting seams. Shorten all long spikes.
